title: test_run.sh exists to validate run.sh behavior across shells
answers: How do I test changes to the Docker entrypoint script?
Is there a script to check run.sh still works after editing it?
How was run.sh verified to behave the same under ash vs bash?
body: When modifying packaging/docker/run.sh, use packaging/docker/test_run.sh to compare behavior before/after a change (introduced in this PR to verify ash/dash parity after removing the bash dependency). Run it against the modified script to catch regressions in env-var parsing, AWS profile handling, secrets-from-file, and plugin installation logic before shipping.
says: How do I verify Docker startup script changes work across shells?
Does the entrypoint still function after modifying the run script?
Testing shell script compatibility for different shell environments
Catching environment variable parsing bugs before deploying Docker
Validating startup behavior for ash and bash parity
search: packaging/docker/test_run.sh validates run.sh behavior across shells (ash, dash, bash) and must be run after modifying packaging/docker/run.sh to catch regressions. It tests environment variable parsing, AWS profile handling, secrets-from-file loading, and plugin installation logic. Use it before shipping changes to verify compatibility, especially after removing bash dependencies to ensure ash/dash parity.
